Master Circular on Personal Loans/Finance 
(Annexure to Circular No. BM 1213 dated February 13, 2025) 
Page 1 of 16 
 
1. 
Coverage 
 
1.1 
Broadly, ‘Personal Loans/finance’ (PL) are defined as loans/finance that 
are granted to individuals for non-business purposes.  
 
 
 
1.2 
The nature of facilities could include all fund-based outstanding facilities 
and may be in the form of term loans/finance, overdrafts, credit card 
facilities, etc. 
 
1.3 
‘Personal 
Loans/finance’ 
are 
further 
categorised 
as 
‘Personal 
Loans/finance Against Salary’ (PLAS) and ‘Other Personal Loans/finance’ 
(OPL) 
 
1.4 
‘Personal Loans/finance Against Salary’ (PLAS) should be further 
categorized by the banks, as under:

1.5 
In case of purchase of land, the borrower should undertake to complete 
the construction within a period of 3 years from the date of purchase. 
Banks should put in place a mechanism to follow-up with the borrowers. 

 
 
 
 
Master Circular on Personal Loans/Finance 
(Annexure to Circular No. BM 1213 dated February 13, 2025) 
Page 2 of 16 
 
 
1.6 
Personal Loans/finance granted to staff are exempted from the above-
mentioned categorization. 
 
 
1.7 
OPL: Personal Loans granted to individuals for non-business purposes not 
based on ‘Salary’ fall under this category. The DBR/tenor/interest rate 
requirements stipulated herein do not apply for this category of loans. 
However, the credit policy of the bank should lay down appropriate 
aggregate and individual borrower limits.  
2. 
Prudential Ceilings for ‘Personal Loans/Finance’ 
 
2.1. 
Overall Quantitative Ceiling: 
 
2.1.1 The overall ‘Personal Loan’ (PLAS and OPL) portfolio of the bank, 
including IBEs, should not exceed 50% of the Total Credit. The sub-limits 
for HL and GPL are left to the discretion of the banks. Accordingly, the 
Board of the bank should set the sub-limits in their credit policy based on 
the risk appetite of the bank, the adherence to which should be 
monitored by risk management and compliance functions and 
reviewed by internal audit.  
 
2.2. 
Tenor: 
 
2.2.1 The tenor should not exceed: 
 
Type  
Maximum Tenor 
GPL  
10 years or till the age of 70 years, whichever is earlier 
HL  
25 years or till the age of 70 years, whichever is earlier 
OAS 
One year 
 
2.2.2 Banks are permitted to grant personal loans up to the age of 70 years, 
irrespective of whether the borrower is a salaried individual or a 
pensioner, subject to adherence to the tenor and debt-burden ratio (as 
applicable to the salaried individual or pensioner). In other words, banks 
are permitted to grant personal loans to salaried individual up to 70 years 
by reckoning the net monthly salary and the expected net monthly 
pension, provided that the respective loan tenor and debt burden ratio 
requirements are duly met. In such cases, due care should be exercised 
in reckoning the ‘expected net monthly pension’ to avoid risks of over 
estimation. Banks should rely on information provided by reliable sources 
such as the website/portal of Social Protection Fund (SPF), noting to 
maintain records for verification by audit/examination. 
 

 
 
 
 
Master Circular on Personal Loans/Finance 
(Annexure to Circular No. BM 1213 dated February 13, 2025) 
Page 3 of 16 
 
 
2.2.3 The tenors stipulated above are the ceilings and should not be treated 
as entitlements. While granting loans/finance, banks may consider 
having some cushion in tenor to take care of underlying risks (including 
rise in interest/profit rates).  Hence, exceeding of stipulated tenor is not 
permitted during the tenor of the loans/finance and, accordingly, while 
sanctioning the loan/finance, banks should take into account such 
factors. 
 
2.3 Debt burden ratio:

2.3.2 The higher DBR limits for HL for borrowers with ‘net monthly salary/net 
pension of OMR 3500 and above is subject to: 
  
2.3.2.1 
Compliance with the 50%/40% ceiling for DBR for GPL. 
 
2.3.2.2 
Detailed credit review of the borrower as per the credit policy 
of the bank, noting that the higher limit is only the ceiling and 
the actual DBR should reflect the credit risk. 
 
 
 

 
 
 
 
Master Circular on Personal Loans/Finance 
(Annexure to Circular No. BM 1213 dated February 13, 2025) 
Page 4 of 16 
 
 
2.3.2.3 
Sufficient disposable income is available to the borrower for 
maintenance of self/ family after deduction of monthly 
instalment and 
 
2.3.2.4 
Ensuring avoidance of the risk of overestimation, as mentioned 
in para 2.2.2.) 
 
2.3.3 Debt burden for the above purposes should reckon all debt obligations, 
including credit cards and overdrafts, if any. 
 
2.3.4 Banks should take due care in determining the overall debt burden of 
the borrowers (including the borrowings with Finance and Leasing 
Companies) by reference to such sources like Mala’a, account history, 
credit history, disposable income available to the borrower for 
maintenance of self/family after deduction of monthly instalment, etc. 
 
2.3.5 Net Salary/Net Pension Salary is the actual amount received by the bank 
regularly and one-off receipts should not be reckoned for computation 
of DBR. In the case of a borrower with pension and salary (due to new 
job, post-retirement), both pension and salary can be reckoned as 
‘income’, subject to compliance with all applicable quantitative 
ceilings.  
 
2.3.6 While granting personal loan/finance to a salaried individual with a tenor 
beyond the age of retirement (subject to adherence to maximum 
tenor), banks should exercise utmost diligence and prudence in 
reckoning the ‘expected net pension’ of the borrower. 
 
2.3.7 Computing ‘debt-burden ratio’ based upon ‘future statutory increase’ is 
not permitted. In other words, ‘debt-burden ratio’ should be computed 
based on evidenced current net salary/income/pension salary.     
 
2.3.8 ‘Other income’ can be reckoned for computing DBR only if it is verifiable 
and there is reasonable certainty of receipt for the entire tenor of the 
loan/finance and banks should maintain adequate documentary proof, 
thereof.  
 
2.3.9 In the case of overdrafts granted against salary (OAS), the minimum 
monthly debt-burden should be one-twelfth of the overdraft limit, 
however banks may consider a more conservative norm. 

 
 
 
 
Master Circular on Personal Loans/Finance 
(Annexure to Circular No. BM 1213 dated February 13, 2025) 
Page 5 of 16 
 
 
 
2.3.10 In respect of credit card against salary (CCAS), the minimum monthly 
debt-burden should be 5% of the overall credit card limit, however banks 
may consider a more conservative norm. 
 
2.3.11 The DBR stipulated above are the ceilings and should not be treated as 
entitlements. While granting loans/finance, banks may consider having 
some cushion in DBR to take care of underlying risks (including rise in 
interest/profit rates).  Hence, exceeding of DBR is not permitted during 
the tenor of the loans/finance and, accordingly, while sanctioning the 
loan/finance, banks should take into account such factors.  
 
 
2.4 Credit Card and Overdraft Limits: 
 
2.4.1 Credit card limits against salary (CCAS) and Overdraft against salary 
(OAS) should not exceed: 
 
Type  
For non-pensioners 
For Pensioners 
CCAS  
5 times of net salary  2 times of net pension salary 
OAS 
3 times of net salary 
2 times of net pension salary 
 
2.4.2 The overdraft account may be permitted to be operated as a running 
account (with credit and debit balances alternating). 
 
2.4.3 Overdraft against salary (OAS – hereinafter referred as ‘overdraft’) when 
sanctioned should not be for a period of more than one year. In other 
words, the closing balance in overdraft account should be in credit at 
least for one full day anytime during the period of one-year tenor after 
the sanctioned overdraft amount is drawn, partly or fully. 
 
2.4.4 Automatic renewal of overdraft is not permitted. Any renewal of 
overdraft should be subject to compliance with credit appraisal as per 
credit policy and the instructions issued herein, such as the account 
being in credit balance at least one full day any time during the tenor 
(as per para 2.4.3 above) and being within the stipulated DBR. 
 
 

 
 
 
 
Master Circular on Personal Loans/Finance 
(Annexure to Circular No. BM 1213 dated February 13, 2025) 
Page 6 of 16 
 
 
 
2.5 Interest/profit Rate Ceiling and application: 
 
2.5.1 Interest/profit rates on different categories of ‘Personal Loan/finance’ 
should not exceed 
 
Type  
Ceiling Interest/profit Rate * 
HL, GPL and OAS  
6% 
CCAS 
18% 
 
(* the interest rate ceiling is subject to change, from time to time) 
 
2.5.2 The interest/profit rate shall be effective rate of interest/profit payable 
on reducing balances. In other words, there shall be no reference to flat 
rate of interest/profit.  
 
2.5.3 The interest/profit rate may be fixed or variable. However, the bank 
should advise the borrower, beforehand, the options available (if 
provided by the bank) and also provide the expected repayment 
schedule in both cases.  
 
2.5.4 In the case of variable interest/profit rate loans/finance, the terms of 
offer should also contain the basis on which the bank will change the 
interest/profit rate along with periodicity of review. 
 
2.5.5 Changes in interest/profit rate (for variable interest/profit rate-based 
loans/finance) should be intimated to the borrowers two months before 
the date of its effect.  
 
 
2.5.6 The basis on which the interest/profit rate is changed (variable 
interest/profit rate) should be fair, reasonable, predictable and based 
on a pre-determined formula. The details of resetting process (for 
variable interest/profit rates) and monthly interest/profit rates (both for 
fixed and variable) should be published in the homepage of the website 
of the bank, on a monthly basis. 
 
2.5.7 Any repricing of loans/finance (variable interest/profit rate personal 
loans/finance) should not result in non-compliance of maximum 
permitted DBR or Tenor.  
 
Hence, banks are advised to operate well within the permitted 
DBR/Tenor/Interest rate/Profit rate and have sufficient cushion for 
interest/profit rate movements.  
 

 
 
 
 
Master Circular on Personal Loans/Finance 
(Annexure to Circular No. BM 1213 dated February 13, 2025) 
Page 7 of 16 
 
 
2.5.8 “Teaser Loan/finance” or ‘step-up interest/profit rate’ or loan/finance 
with similar features are not permitted. In other words, setting 
interest/profit rates at lower levels in the initial period and increased 
interest/profit rates at a later period is not permitted.   
 
2.5.9 In respect of conventional banks, overdue or penal interest, if any, 
should not exceed 1% p.a., and should be on the overdue amount and 
for overdue period only (Installments waived at bank’s instance shall not 
be treated as overdue). 
 
2.5.10 In respect of Islamic Banking Entities (IBEs), penalty on defaults can be 
charged subject to the following: 
 
2.5.10.1 There should be clarity and prior understanding with the 
borrower. 
 
2.5.10.2 The maximum penalty that can be imposed is subject to a 
ceiling of 1% p.a. of overdue amount and period. 
 
2.5.10.3 Such charges are imposed with the objective to deter the 
borrower from making willful default. 
 
2.5.10.4 Recoveries of such charges should be donated to the charity 
fund maintained by the IBE and should not form part of the 
income.    
 
2.5.11 While the extant stipulated interest/profit rate ceilings on personal 
loans/finance/credit cards shall apply, licensed banks are encouraged 
to charge less than the maximum stipulated ceiling rate to pensioners.  
 
2.6 Margins / Loan to Value (LTV) Ratio 
 
2.6.1 The margin/LTV Ratio requirements for different types of PL are as under: 
 
Type  
Minimum margin 
Vehicle Loans/finance (VL) 
20% 
GPL for purchase of shares including 
subscription to Initial Public Offers (IPOs) 
50% 
 
 
 

 
 
 
 
Master Circular on Personal Loans/Finance 
(Annexure to Circular No. BM 1213 dated February 13, 2025) 
Page 8 of 16 
 
 
Type  
Loan to Value Ratio 
Housing Loan (HL) 
90% 
 
2.6.2 In the case of Housing Loans, the cost of land owned by the borrower 
and subsidy (if any) received from the Government for the related 
housing project can be treated as margin while computing LTV Ratio. 
 
2.6.3 Additionally, in respect of all housing loans/finance, the cost of 
registration and insurance can be included in the value of the housing 
property while computing the LTV Ratio, subject to compliance with the 
applicable DBR requirements. 
 
2.6.4 Further, in respect of all other types of Personal Loan (GPL), the cost of 
insurance premium, if financed by the bank, is subject to adherence to 
the maximum DBR as well as applicable margin requirements.  
 
3 
Personal Loan/finance (non-housing) Top Up 
 
3.1 
Top-up Loans/Finance, including grant of additional loans, are permitted 
only after 24 months of satisfactory conduct of existing loan/finance or 
after 50% of existing loan/finance is repaid or when the eligibility 
prescribed in para 2.3.1 was not availed at the time of origination of 
loan.  
 
3.2 
In case a customer applies for a new loan/finance for an amount higher 
than the outstanding of the current loan/finance and requests for 
closure of the old loan/finance, such cases should also be treated as 
top-up of loan/finance. 
 
4 
Deferrals 
 
4.1 
Deferrals, if any, extended by banks in respect of non-housing Personal 
Loans are subject to the following: 
  
4.1.1 A maximum of two Eid-related deferrals per calendar year (referred 
herein as ‘bank-offered deferral’) could be offered, which will not come 
under 
the 
purview 
of 
‘guidelines 
on 
restructuring’ 
(Ref: 
BSD/2016/BKUP/Banks & FLCs/447 dated April 7, 2016). 
 
 
 

 
 
 
 
Master Circular on Personal Loans/Finance 
(Annexure to Circular No. BM 1213 dated February 13, 2025) 
Page 9 of 16 
 
 
4.1.2 Any other deferrals, in all situations, offered by the bank should be in 
compliance with the ‘guidelines on restructuring’ and applicable 
classification norms. 
 
4.1.3 Further, the ‘bank-offered deferrals’ should not result in extension of 
tenor of the loan/finance beyond the maximum tenor stipulated for the 
respective category of borrower and/or beyond the age of 70 years, 
whichever is earlier. 
 
4.1.4 All deferrals (including Eid-related deferrals) can be given only after 
customer gives the consent. In other words, banks are not permitted to 
offer the deferrals automatically. 
  
4.2 
No moratorium or payment holidays can be offered in respect of 
Personal Loans/Finance either at the beginning or during the tenor of the 
loan/finance unless the customer desires restructuring, which should be 
undertaken in compliance with ‘guidelines on restructuring’. Grant of 
‘Eid waivers’ will not be treated as moratorium or payment holidays.    
 
4.3 
The financial impact of deferral should be advised, transparently, to the 
customers, beforehand, in case customer opts for deferral by providing 
the customer, in each instance, with a revised Key Fact Statement (KFS) 
and revised repayment schedule, as instructed in para 14.1 and 14.2 
herein. 
5 
Charges 
 
5.1 
Processing fees shall not exceed OMR 25/- in respect of GPL and OMR 
50/- in respect of HL. There shall be no processing charges for Pensioners 
with net monthly pension less than OMR 1000/-. Further, Central Bank 
expects banks to consider waiving fully or partially the processing 
charges in respect of all pensioners.   
 
5.2 
Prepayment/pre-closure (early settlement) fee should not be charged 
when loans/finance are topped up or consolidated or restructured or in 
circumstances when there is no prepayment effectively. 
 
5.3 
Administrative fees/charges for “credit life insurance/takaful” should not 
exceed 0.05% of loan/finance amount subject to a minimum of OMR 5/- 
and a maximum of OMR 75/- on personal or housing loan/finance 
insurance. No other tie-up, in whatsoever manner, should have scope to 
make/hide prohibited charges. In other words, (maximum) fee 
prescribed hereunder should be the only accrual on loan/finance 
related arrangements, if any.  

 
 
 
 
Master Circular on Personal Loans/Finance 
(Annexure to Circular No. BM 1213 dated February 13, 2025) 
Page 10 of 16 
 
 
5.4 
Prepayment charges (early settlement charges), if any, for non-
pensioners and pensioners with net monthly pension of above OMR 
1000/-, should not exceed 1% of the prepaid amount. In respect of 
pensioners with net monthly pension up to OMR 1000/-, licensed banks 
should not charge/levy prepayment charges (early settlement charges) 
in case of partial or full repayment of the loan/finance or in case of 
takeover of the loan/finance by other banks/FLCs. 
 
5.5 
The initial issuance fee and annual renewal membership fee for credit 
cards should not exceed OMR 50, based on the type of cards and 
additional benefits provided to the customers. In respect of high-end 
cards with several premium benefits, the issuance/renewal fee may be 
fixed higher than OMR 50, subject to: 
 
5.5.1 
The issuance/renewal fee should reflect the premium benefits 
provided to the customers. 
 
5.5.2 
The per card fee charged by card issuing association and the 
mark-up added by the bank should be clearly documented, 
and should be available for verification by audit/examination. 
 
5.5.3 
The mark-up should be reasonable and fair. 
 
5.5.4 
Customer should be informed about the charges, beforehand, 
as per the requirement given in Financial Consumer Protection 
Regulatory Framework (FCPRF).  
 
5.6 
While the charges mentioned in the foregoing paragraphs are the 
ceilings, banks should not consider them as entitlements and should 
strive to offer concessional charges to the pensioners.  
 
6 
Exceeding DBR/Tenor in Exceptional Situations 
 
6.1 
Banks may restructure existing personal loans/finance beyond DBR and 
tenor requirements in exceptional situations, on a case-to-case basis. 
These exceptional situations may include, but not limited to – job-losses; 
wage-reduction; early retirement; medical emergencies of the borrower 
or a family member; family situations such as death, divorce or 
imprisonment of the breadwinner in the household etc.  
 
 

 
 
 
 
Master Circular on Personal Loans/Finance 
(Annexure to Circular No. BM 1213 dated February 13, 2025) 
Page 11 of 16 
 
 
6.2 
The Board of Directors of the bank should formulate an appropriate 
policy for ‘Exceeding the Stipulated DBR/Tenor by Restructuring of the 
Personal Loans’, wherein it should define the aforementioned and other 
exceptional situations for restructuring of the existing facility, while 
satisfying itself about the prospects of recovery of the loan.  
 
6.3 
The genuineness in such cases should be well established and 
documented, and the permission granted by appropriate approval 
authority (not below the rank of AGM in case of local banks and CEO in 
the case of foreign banks) with necessary controls.  
 
6.4 
It should be ensured that the borrower has the repayment capacity and 
the residual ‘take-home’ salary/income is sufficient and is not unduly 
burdened by the revised terms of the debt. 
 
6.5 
Relaxations from the DBR/tenor should be provided only to the extent of 
genuine requirement, adequately assessed by the bank, and is subject 
to the fulfillment of other requirements specified herein.  
 
6.6 
In principle, banks are not permitted to provide additional or top-up of 
loans/finance in such cases. However, only in justifiable and well-
deserved cases, banks are granted discretion to allow a top-up of 
loans/finance, on a judicious basis.  
 
6.7 
No marketing/campaign/promotion, of any sort, in any media, is 
permitted in this regard. 
 
6.8 
The revised tenor in any case should not extend beyond the age of 70 
years of the borrower.  
 
6.9 
There should be compliance with all extant instructions on ‘restructuring 
of loans/finance’ and applicable IFRS-9 guidelines. 
 
6.10 Robust mechanisms should be put in place for follow-up with such 
borrowers to get notified on the change of job/change of income and 
to ensure prompt recovery. In such cases, while revising the repayment 
schedule, banks should endeavor to comply with the DBR/tenor 
stipulations.  
 
6.11 Banks should not direct their borrowers to approach the Central Bank for 
obtaining the exemptions, which is not a desirable practice.  
 

 
 
 
 
Master Circular on Personal Loans/Finance 
(Annexure to Circular No. BM 1213 dated February 13, 2025) 
Page 12 of 16 
 
 
6.12 A record containing the list of such approvals with details including 
reasons for restructuring and the approval authority along with 
justification for the relaxation should be maintained by the banks, for 
verification by audit/examination. 
 
7. 
Credit Risk Management 
 
7.1 
Banks should develop a credit policy with strong credit standards, duly 
approved by the Board, and internal guidelines, procedures and 
controls for the grant of personal loan/finance.  
 
7.2 
The credit 
policy 
should 
also factor 
the ‘financial 
inclusion’ 
objectives/mandates of the Central Bank by devising appropriate and 
suitable Personal Loan products for different segments especially, 
pensioners and low-income group (defined as borrower with ‘net salary’ 
of OMR 500 and below) subject to adequate risk management 
procedures.  
 
7.3 
The ‘credit policy’ of the bank for personal loans/finance should, among 
others, include the following: 
 
7.3.1 The types of ‘other income’ which can be reckoned for granting 
of personal loans/finance and the extent to which it can be 
reckoned based on reasonable certainty of income.  
 
7.3.2 The extent of cushion to be kept in Tenor/DBR (stipulated in 
paragraphs 2.2.3 and 2.3.11, herein) for various scenarios. 
 
 
8. 
Takeover of Personal Loans/finance 
 
8.1 
Banks are permitted to takeover personal loans/finance from other 
banks/FLCs as per the credit policy of the bank, however, the category 
of the loan should be retained and there should be compliance with the 
instructions issued herein. In other words, the bank which takes over the 
personal loan should not re-categorise it, except in cases permitted 
under para 10.1.  
 
8.2 
Shari’a compliance from all aspects should be ensured in respect of 
takeover of personal loans/finance by Islamic Banking Entities.  
 
 

 
 
 
 
Master Circular on Personal Loans/Finance 
(Annexure to Circular No. BM 1213 dated February 13, 2025) 
Page 13 of 16 
 
 
 
9. 
Consolidation of Personal Loans/finance 
 
9.1 
Consolidation of loans should not be undertaken to regularize past dues 
or to prevent account from slipping into non-performing loans and 
should be undertaken only for the operational convenience of the 
customer. 
 
9.2 
In respect of consolidation of loans/finance (within the bank or during 
the take-over of loans/finance), the categorization of loans/finance 
should remain intact and non-housing personal loans/finance and 
housing loans/finance should not be consolidated into a single loan, 
except in cases permitted under para 10.1.  
 
9.3 
In the case of takeover or consolidation or top-up of personal 
loans/finance, the customers should be advised upfront transparently, in 
writing, on the additional costs (charges, insurance, etc.) to be borne by 
them. 
 
9.4 
The aforesaid consolidation of personal loan/finance will not be treated 
as restructuring of the loan/finance. 
 
 
10. 
Re-categorisation of Personal Loan/finance 
 
10.1 Conversion of a personal loan obtained and utilized for housing 
purposes can be re-categorised as housing loan, including at the time 
of take-over, only if there is very clear documentary evidence for 
utilization of loan proceeds for housing purposes.  
 
10.2 Such re-categorisation should be permitted by an official/authority one 
level above the sanctioning authority for Personal loan/finance.  
 
 
11. 
Credit-Life Insurance 
 
11.1 ‘Credit life insurance/Takaful’ arrangements for personal loans/finance 
should be subject to instructions issued by the Central Bank from time to 
time.  
 
11.2 The customers should be made aware of the availability of choice to 
them to arrange for ‘credit life insurance’ by themselves and its 
acceptability by the bank, in a prominent and effective manner.  
 
 

 
 
 
 
Master Circular on Personal Loans/Finance 
(Annexure to Circular No. BM 1213 dated February 13, 2025) 
Page 14 of 16 
 
 
 
11.3 In case of closure of loan due to maturity or pre-payment (early 
settlement) or grant of additional/top-up of loans/finance, bank should 
facilitate automatic refund of insurance/takaful premium for the 
unexpired 
maturity 
wherever 
the 
bank 
has 
arranged 
the 
insurance/takaful. In other words, bank should not wait for the customer 
to seek/apply for refund and should put in place a process accordingly 
to initiate/facilitate refund even where insurance/takaful is arranged by 
the customers themselves.  
 
11.4 In the case of vehicle loans/finance, banks should ensure that there is 
credit-life insurance (bank arranged or customer arranged, as per the 
choice of the customer). However, banks should not insist upon 
comprehensive insurance.  
 
 
12. 
End-use Requirements 
 
12.1 End-use of disbursed funds should be ascertained, recorded and 
monitored with due diligence. Purpose of (non-housing) personal 
loan/finance shall be non-business. 
 
 
13 
Guarantors 
 
13.1 The terms and conditions applicable to guarantors should be clear and 
there should be compliance with applicable Laws of the Sultanate. In 
this regard, there should be compliance with the contents of Royal 
Decree No. 75/2010, which states as follows: 
 
“In the commercial guarantee for the personal bank loan, it is permissible 
to ask the guarantor to include in the guarantee contract a term 
obligating the creditor to dispossess the debtor first and before reverting 
to the guarantor”.

14.2 The borrowers should be advised upfront, of the important terms and 
conditions (referred as Key Fact Statement (KFS) in para 1.3.7 of Financial 
Consumer Protection Regulatory Framework (FCPRF) attached with 
Circular No. BM 1184 dated December 29, 2021) in a transparent 
manner. Banks should also provide the borrowers with KFS, loan 
agreement and repayment schedule in Arabic or English, as per their 
choice. 
 
14.3 Whenever there is a change in the terms and conditions, involving 
change in tenor or DBR or interest-rate or insurance or offer of 
waivers/deferrals, the borrower should be provided a revised KFS and 
revised repayment schedule, under acknowledgement. 
 
14.4 Personal loans/finance/finance against own ‘Term Deposits’ will be 
outside the purview of these restrictions. However, such loans/finance 
will be subject to the overall quantitative ceilings referred in para 2.1 
above.  
 
14.5 Joint account loans/finance against joint salaries may be considered 
provided the joint account holders are severally and jointly legally liable 
for the obligation incurred. There should be commensurate care, subject 
to compliance with instructions provided herein and the provisions of 
‘Oman Commercial Law’. Accordingly, banks should draw up the 
agreement between themselves and the joint account holders, 
transparently mentioning the responsibilities and liabilities of the joint 
account holders.   
 
14.6 Banks should issue balance confirmation/no-due/no-liability certificates 
on personal loans/finance within a maximum period of five working days 
from the date of receipt of request from the customer.  
 
14.7 Any campaigns and promotions related to personal loans/finance 
should conform to the instructions provided in Circular No. BM 1167 
dated November 11, 2019 to the extent that they are not in 
contradiction with the instructions given herein.

15 
Reporting Requirements 
 
15.1 There should be appropriate Management Information System (MIS) to 
capture detailed and granular data on Personal Loans/finance (e.g., 
category-wise, gender-wise, salary range-wise, wilayat-wise, purpose-
wise, amount-wise, interest/profit-rate wise, maturity-wise, and any 
combination thereof). Banks should be in readiness to provide such data 
to the Central Bank, at any time. 
 
15.2 PLAS should be reported in item B.1 of monthly Banking Return RD-3 and 
in item 24 of RD-15.
